name: Covered Bridge (Cedarburg, Wisconsin)
facts: The Covered Bridge, built in 1876, spans Cedar Creek with a 120‑foot timber lattice truss, originally constructed entirely from oak and pine without bolts or nails.
In 1962, county engineers relocated the historic bridge 50 feet east to preserve it, restricting traffic to pedestrians and building a modern vehicular bridge just yards to the west.
The bridge earned its place on the National Register of Historic Places on March 14, 1973, and a 1955 DAR plaque proudly declares it the "last covered bridge in Wisconsin."
